metadata.title: Read the Section Before You Place the Figure
metadata.note: Week 7 how-to video. Voice hai/Bella for @HumanitariansAI. Content only from the image-placement chat and an earlier report; no claim about when any figure was placed.
metadata.author: Risa Samanta

beats.narration_text: Placing a figure is not just pasting an image. Where it goes, which caption it carries, and whether it is approved all matter. This is Risa Samanta's how-to video for the week: placing a figure in an MDX chapter.

props.command: claude "place these two checkpoint figures in the chapter, using the reviewer-approved captions"

beats.role_note: a figure block, from the chat
beats.narration_text: A figure in these chapters is three things: an image path, an alt text, and a caption that begins with the figure number. The caption comes from the reviewer-finalized text, not from a guess.

props.title: a figure block in MDX
props.code: Figure 26.2.X: CTLA-4 Pathway: CTLA-4 is an inhibitory receptor on T cells that competes with CD28 for binding to B7-1 and B7-2 on antigen-presenting cells (APCs). ...

beats.role_note: three homes for the same two images
beats.narration_text: The same two checkpoint figures had three different homes. The tracking sheet said chapter twenty-five, but those sections cover target validation and TKI classification, with no checkpoint content at all. Earlier drafts used chapter sixteen. The latest instructions say chapter twenty-six, sections twenty-six point two point two and twenty-six point two point three. The only way to know is to read the destination section before you place the figure.
beats.visual_intent: Real drifted caption names from the actual repo animating toward a clean sectioned scheme. Show the mechanism, not a count.

props.file: where do the two checkpoint figures go?
props.caption: read the destination section before placing

beats.narration_text: Some figures are not ready. A lung screening image had gone through several failed correction rounds, and the last note on it still said to check the comments. The right move was to hold off placing it until a version was approved. Likewise, the CTLA-4 figure had to be the corrected version, with the thymus element removed, before it went live.

props.command: claude "is this image approved? check the comments before you place it"

beats.narration_text: The figure number in the caption was left as a placeholder, X and Y here, until the position was settled, because the book's numbering comes from where a figure sits. Place the figure first, and let the number follow.

props.title: captions with placeholder numbers
props.code:
Figure 26.2.X: CTLA-4 Pathway
Figure 26.2.Y: PD-1/PD-L1 Pathway

# X and Y stay until the position is settled

beats.narration_text: The habit is four steps. Read the section the figure is going into. Check that the image is approved and is the corrected version. Use the reviewer's caption. Then place it.

props.command: claude "before placing, tell me whether this figure belongs in this section, and whether the image is approved"

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Before you let an AI place figures, give it the destination text, ask it to say whether each figure belongs there, and ask it to flag any image still marked not approved. Then read its flags before you accept a single placement.

props.command: claude "here is the destination section. say whether the figure belongs here, and flag any image marked not approved"

beats.narration_text: Read the section before you place the figure. This has been Risa Samanta's how-to, voiced by Bella for Humanitarians AI. Read the flags before you accept a placement.
